3559:

3561:
** νουμην-ία**, ἡ,
_Attic dialect_ _contraction_ for **νεομηνία** (which occurs in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 4.35, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.57 (_plural_), “PMag.Leid.W.” 1.28,9.43 (_plural_), 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 14.298)}}:—also **νευμηνία**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|“SIG” 1106.19 (Cos, 4th-3rd c.BC)}}; **νεμονηΐα**, {{Refs|“GDI” 5015.28, +others (from Crete)}}; **νομενία**, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PCair.Zen.” 167.5 (3rd c.BC)}}:— **new moon: the first of the month,** Pi.[same place], {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator “fragment” 58 (_plural_), 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 43, “Ach.” 999 (_plural_)}}, etc.; ν. κατὰ σελήνην to denote the **true** or **natural new moon,** as opposed to to the νουμηνία of the calendars, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.28; also ἡ κατὰ θεὸν ν. “PMag.Par.” 1.787, 2389}}; ν. τοῦ ἔτους, of the spring equinox, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 91.}}
3562:
Included with: ** νουνεχ-ής**, ές,
(ἔχω) **with understanding, sensible, discreet,** Ps.-{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1132.48, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.48.8 (_superlative_)}}; λογισμός {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|[prev. author] 3.105.9, compare 2nd c.AD: Ptolemaeus Mathematicus “Tetrabiblos” 164}}; τὸ νουνεχές, = {νουνέχεια}, [{{Refs|Anonymus cited in 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus see {ἀνεῖτο}}}]. _adverb_ **-χῶς**{{NT+4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1436b33, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.83.3, +others, 2nd c.BC: Agatharchides Geographus 63, NT.Mark.12.34, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 10.267.}}

3570:
** νῡνί**,
_Attic dialect_ form of νῦν, strengthened by -ῑ _demonstrative_, **now, at this moment,** mostly of **the present,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Inscriptiones Graecae 12.98.3, etc.: frequently in Comedy texts, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 325, “Ra.” 290, 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 41, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἥρως” 27, etc.}}: less frequently with past tenses, ὧν ν. διέβαλλε {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.14; ν. συνεληλύθαμεν 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 6.7; ν. ἐβουλήθη 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.20; ν. βοηθήσαντες συνκατετάττοντο “IG” 22.237.11 (4th c.BC)}}: also with _future_, ν. δὲ πειράσομαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.25, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 18.35}}: with _aorist_ _imperative_, ν. μεταγνώτω {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.92}}: rarely in the sense, **as the case stands** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|compare (νῦν 1.4), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.129, 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator “fragment” 31.—Never in Trag. (5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 306 is corrupt): Comedy texts also have νυνμενί, for νυνὶ μέν, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 448}}; νυνδί, for νυνὶ δέ, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Eq.” 1357, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 190.16}}; compare νυνγαρί, for νυνὶ γάρ, {{Refs|12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 45.3.}}

3587:
** ξῠρ-έω**,
Trag. and _Attic dialect_ (see. below); **ξῠράω**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.180b, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 1.22}} (also in _present_ _middle_, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.84, 4th c.AD: Palaephatus Paradoxographus 32}}, and _present_ _passive_, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Cyn.” 14)}}; both forms in codices of {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus}}; compare ξύρω: _future_ **-ήσω**{{LXX|LXX.Deu.21.12}}: _aorist_ ἐξύρησα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ παθῶν” 4, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.35, etc.}}:—_middle_, _future_ ξυρήσομαι {{LXX+1st c.AD+|LXX.Eze.44.20, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 2.15.1, 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus}} see at {πριαμωθήσομαι}: _aorist_ ἐξυρησάμην {{LXX+2nd c.AD+|LXX.Num.6.19, +others, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMeretr.” 12.5}}:—_passive_, _future_ **-ηθήσομαι**{{LXX|LXX.Lev.13.33:}}_perfect_ ἐξύρημαι (see. below): (ξυρόν):—**shave,** ξυροῦντες (variant{-ῶντες}) τῶν παιδίων τὴν κεφαλήν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.65: with double _accusative_, ξυρήσας μιν τὰς τρίχας [prev. author] 5.35: proverbial of danger or pain, ξυρεῖ γὰρ ἐν χρῷ}} **it shaves** close, 'touches the quick', {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 786}}; ξυρεῖν ἐπιχειρεῖν λέοντα, of a dangerous undertaking, 'beard the lion', {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 341c}}:—_middle_ and _passive_, **shave oneself** or **have oneself shaved,** ξυρεῦνται (variant{-ῶνται}) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.36}}; ἐξυρημένος [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. passage], 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 191; ξυρούμενον 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 264: also with _accusative_, ξυρεῦνται (variant{-ῶνται}) πᾶν τὸ σῶμα}}] they **shave their** whole body or **have** it **shaved,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.37; τὰς ὀφρύας, τὴν κεφαλήν, [prev. work] 66}}; ἐξυρημένος τὴν κεφαλήν **with** one's head **shaved,** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Merc.Cond.” 1.}}
3589:
** ὀγδο-ήκοντα**, οἱ, αἱ, τά,
_indeclinable_, **eighty,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.47, etc.}}: _Ionic dialect_ and _Doric dialect_ **ὀγδώκοντα** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.568, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.163, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 4.34}}; **ὀδώκοντα** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“Ostr.” 323.6 (2nd c.BC).}}
3590:
** ὄγδοος**, η, ον,
**eighth,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.223, etc.}}; ὀγδόη (i.e. ἡμέρα), ὀγδόῃ τῆς πρυτανείας {{Refs 1st c.AD+|“IG” 12.374.416; ὀγδόῃ Πυανεψιῶνος 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Theseus” 36. [ὄγδοον}} as _disyllable_, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 7.261 = 14.287 (assuming variant): ὄγδος late spelling in “Ostr.” 922, etc.]}}
3594:
** ὁδηγ-έω**,
**lead** one **upon his way, guide,** with _accusative_ _person_, {{NT+5th c.BC+|1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 24, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 728, NT.Act.8.31, 2nd c.AD(?): Xenophon Ephesius Scriptor Eroticus 1.9: _absolutely_, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1402; φύσιος εἰς τὸ ἄριστον -εούσης 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “νόμος” 2}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.954b}}, Vett. Val.359.30:— also **ὁδηγ-ετέω**, {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Themistius Sophista “Orationes” 11.151c.}}
3595:
** ὁδηγ-ός**, ὁ,
**guide,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 5.5.15, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Alexander” 27}}; of a goddess, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Pausanias Periegeta 2.11.2}}; part of a dirigible χελώνη, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Athenaeus Mechanicus 34.6; ταῖς Ἀριστοτελείοις τέχναις ὁδηγοῖς χρησάμενος 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Amm.” 1.12, compare 1st c.BC: Philodemus Philosophus “περὶ παρρησίας” p.20 O.: as}} _adjective_, ὁδηγὰ πλοῖα **pilot**-boats, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|“Sammelb.” 7173.16 (2nd c.AD).}}
3596:
** ὁδοιπορ-έω**,
_imperfect_ ὡδοιπόρεον,-ουν, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.116}} (variant{ὁ-}), {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1027}}: _future_ **-ήσω**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 58}}: _perfect_ ὁδοιπόρηκα {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Philippides Comicus 13}}: _pluperfect_ _3rd.pers._ _plural_ διοδοιπορήκεσαν {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 8.129}}:—_passive_, _perfect_ ὡδοιπόρηται {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Herm.” 2}}:— **walk,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.110, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 801; ὀρθότεροι -ήσουσι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus}} [prev. cited]; ἐπ᾽ ἄκρων ὁ. **walk** on tiptoe, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1230}}; **come,** ὁ ξένος.. ὧδ᾽ ὁδοιπορεῖ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] “OC” 1251: with _accusative_ _cognate_, ὁδοιπορεῖν ὁδόν 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.116}}; ὁ. τοὺς τόπους **walk over** this ground, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1027.}} — Used in Trag. and _Ionic dialect_ Prose, = _Attic dialect_ βαδίζ; also in later Prose, {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Act.10.9, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 9.500, “PMag.Lond.” 121.181, 2nd c.AD(?): Xenophon Ephesius Scriptor Eroticus 3.2.}}
3597:
** ὁδοιπορ-ία**,
_Ionic dialect_ -ιη, ἡ, **walking,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|hymnus ad Mercurium 85, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἀγμῶν” 15 (_plural_), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.29, 8.118; ὁδοιπορίαις καὶ δρόμοις γυμνάζειν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.2.10}}; τὸ ἄδηλον τῆς ὁ. the uncertainty of the **journey by road,** {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|POxy. 118v.6 (3rd c.AD)}}; **power of walking,** {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 25.552}}; **journey,** σημαίνειν μέτρον ὁδοιπορίας {{Refs|“IG” 22.2640.}}
